about.diffHeading: How it differs from a habit app
about.goalP1: We develop activities that improve your own habits and also ones that help vulnerable groups. Proposals are welcome from individuals, companies, schools and public institutions alike.
about.goalP2: Rather than betting on one technology, we run several ventures together, tie them to the platform to form an ecosystem, and aim further: to build a village.
about.lead: Everyday life into routine, routine into training.
about.linkPost: for the actual list of activities.
about.seoDesc: Total Training Center is a record-based community platform: it suggests everyday actions as activities, then you log them and get them verified. See how it differs from a habit app.
about.title: About
about.whatP1a: Total Training Center gathers everyday actions and habits into topics, breaks each topic into specific activities, and has you log and verify them after you do them. It is a
about.whatP1c: There are currently {activities} activities across {groups} topics, and we keep developing more.
about.whyP1: Some people find daily life dull. Some say it is not much fun. Far more have something they want to do but never get past the third day. It is not a lack of willpower: deciding what to do uses up the energy, and nothing remains once it is done.
about.whyP2: Total Training Center takes care of both. You pick what to do from a list that is already organized, and what you did stays as verified proof. That record becomes the reason to keep going tomorrow.

diff.beyondBody: Beyond personal habits, we build topics that help vulnerable groups. We are open to working with companies, schools and public institutions.
diff.pickBody: You do not have to design a habit. Pick one from the activities already organized by topic and you have started.
diff.pickTitle: A list you only have to pick from
diff.proofBody: Anyone can tick a checkbox. We ask for an unedited record made right after. A structure that is hard to fool yourself in is what makes a habit last.
diff.togetherBody: Records from people doing the same activity build up alongside yours. Not competition: the sense that you are not the only one is what keeps it going.

guide.howToDesc: From signing up to your first verified activity
guide.howToName: Getting started with Total Training Center
guide.lead: Six steps from sign-up to your first verification.
guide.rejectBody: Too long a gap between doing it and logging it, an edited file, or a format other than the one the activity requires.
guide.seoDesc: Six steps from signing up to your first verified activity, plus what counts as valid proof and which topics to start with.
guide.step1Body: Create an account on the platform. LVL.0 is free and gives you every topic for seven days. You can pick activities straight away, so there is no need to enter payment details first.
guide.step2Body: Before picking activities, read the notices and rules. They cover what counts as valid proof, how records are kept, and how the community is run. Skipping this can get your proof rejected.
guide.step3Body: There are {groups} topics right now. Each has core and optional activities, and each activity states what you need to submit as proof. If this is new to you, start with something low-effort like health and daily habits.
guide.step4Body: Picking a topic assigns its core activities first. Add optional ones if you have room; you do not need many at the start. One activity for a week beats five for three days.
guide.step5Body: Separately from topics, every member automatically gets a set of common activities: {list}. They open and close the day, so they cost little effort but give the day a shape.
guide.step6Body: After doing the activity, upload your record in the required form (photo, video or text). Only two rules: upload right after doing it, and keep the file unedited. Only records that meet both are accepted as proof.
guide.step6Title: Do it and get it verified
guide.step7Body: Miss a day and you do not start over. What you have already logged stays, and you pick it up the next day. The days you missed are part of the record too.
guide.title: Guide

step.accumulateBody: One day of records is nothing. A month of them shows patterns: which weekday you fall off, which topic you keep putting off, what actually stuck. We keep that history in a form you can look back on. The point is to leave it as a record, not a memory.
step.accumulateSummary: As records pile up, you can see who you actually are, in data.
step.performBody: Most activities are things you already do: drink water, eat, sit at your desk. The only change is that you leave a record saying you did. They are sized for five minutes, so weekdays do not break them. Miss a day and the record stays; pick it up tomorrow.
step.performSummary: Put a purpose on what you already do. No extra time required.
step.recordBody: Each activity states its proof format. Tidying uses before-and-after photos, exercise a short video, journalling text, whichever shows the evidence best. The activity screen tells you exactly what to upload, so there is nothing to work out.
step.recordSummary: Photo, video or text, whichever fits the activity.
step.topicBody: Deciding where to start is the hardest part. So instead of a blank screen, we show you an organized list of topics first: health and habits, tidying, meals and cooking, learning, social activity, emotional wellbeing. Each holds activities sized to do today. Pick a topic and you get its core activities, then add as many optional ones as you want.
step.topicSummary: Choose what interests you: health, tidying, meals, learning, relationships, emotions.
step.verifyBody: Two rules. First, upload right after doing it. Second, keep it unedited. A private checklist is easy to tick and move on from; a record that needs evidence is hard to skip. Those two rules are what separate this from a habit app.
step.verifySummary: Right after, unedited. That is what makes a record trustworthy.
